Measured 71.4M vs band max 60M on the dev solve arm — out of band for the first time (58.5M after W12 §1, inside it). The routed water enters every cell's water access downstream of any runoff and a month the land waters — the floodplain, the river, the lake, the routed stream — now counts toward a crop's season, so the static farmed capacity is higher wherever the land is watered (the density ordering's river cells 17.8 → 20.5 persons/km², its rainfed cells 9.8 → 11.6) and the same saturating curve, with no famine variance or mortality, reaches a higher ceiling sooner. At dev P18 is inert by construction — the orographic footprint is zero at 240 wide, where a table cell is smaller than a map cell (third cardinal rule) — so every move on this arm is the paddy's alone: rice's fit rises on flooded ground in the flood months and every other package's falls there by its drowning loss, and nothing else in the grade changed. The river cells of the density ordering read 20.5 → 20.3 persons/km² (the drowning loss on the packages that hold the floodplains, where rice is not yet present), the rain-fed cells 11.6 → 11.6. The corrected hop share is not a tuning: a hop of mean square ⟨d²⟩ delivers s·⟨d²⟩/4 of diffusivity, so the share that delivers D is 4·D·dt/⟨d²⟩ and not D·dt/area. The SAME constants measured 0.670 km/yr at the shipped grid after §1 — inside the band for the first time. Identical physics, two grids: the 167 km reference lattice moves a share of a whole cell's people 167 km in a single hop, so its pulled front outruns the continuum 2·√(r·D) the constants name, where the 42 km shipped lattice does not. Re-measured 2026-09-05 after W14 (P18 and the paddy): −3099, one 84-month stride later; the valley still farms sorghum (staple:nile:solve:dev), whose fit the paddy lowers by the drowning loss on the flooded strip in the flood months — the open question above stands, unchanged in kind.

Measured −2027 vs latest −3500 (−2700 with the grace) on the target solve arm. This row is NEW: before W12 §2 the Indus was reached at −3155, inside the window with the grace (see the pre-§2 reason of arrival:ganges:solve:target). §2 moved every European row EARLIER (Balkans −5654 → −6024, central Europe −3722 → −4683, Rhine −2980 → −4161) and this one 1,128 years LATER, on the same wheat front from the same hearth (36.5°N 37.1°E, −7992). Great-circle from that hearth to each box centre, the legs run at 0.73–0.80 km/yr northwest (Balkans, central Europe, Rhine) and 0.54 east to the Indus, 0.66 before §2. Decided by the per-cell arrival raster (QUESTIONS #64, run on request): it is the Iranian plateau's CAPACITY, not the isotropic split. The eastward leg runs at 0.99–1.06 km/yr for its first 500 km and at 0.85–1.17 on the Indus side, but the rings 1,500–2,000 km from the hearth — median static wheat capacity 0.18–0.20 persons/km², wheat fit 0.06 — cross at 0.16–0.30 km/yr, and that 750 km patch costs ~2,400 years, more than this whole miss. The patch is dry in the substrate because the water that farmed the real piedmont sites (Jeitun, Sang-e Chakhmaq, Mehrgarh, Tepe Yahya: mountain runoff onto alluvial fans) is not represented: their annual moisture reads the quantile map's 0.02 floor, their water access 0.02 with river magnitude 0 within ±125 km, so capacity is starved at both the fertility and the fit — a missing mechanism (DECISIONS P17, routed catchment runoff as water access), not a rate to dial, and not to be reached by lifting the floor. The anisotropy test on the same raster shows no east–west penalty at 30–60°N, so §4/P16 does not buy this row. Why §2 moved it 1,128 years later remains unexplained (no pre-§2 raster). Recorded, not dialed. W13 (2026-09-05) built P17, the routed water, and the watered month; measured on the substrate at this grid without history, the plateau sites barely move (Jeitun 0.02 → 0.07, Mehrgarh 0.02 → 0.12, Sang-e Chakhmaq unchanged) because their catchments hold only the runoff floor in the 1.9° table (DECISIONS P18), while the lower Indus gains wheat outright (Mohenjo-daro 4 → 7 months, capacity 0 → 11.4 persons/km²). This row has NOT been re-measured since W13: the shipped-grid solve arm is v2-long, on request (QUESTIONS #65). Not re-measured since W13 or W14 (the shipped-grid solve arm is v2-long, on request). W14 built P18 — the coarse rain redistributed within each 1.9° table cell by the fine elevation, conserving the cell's total — and measured it on the substrate at this grid, no history: it does NOT lift the plateau sites. Jeitun, Sang-e Chakhmaq, Mehrgarh and Tepe Yahya read annual moisture 0.02 → 0.02 and water access unchanged (0.02, 0.02, 0.12, 0.07), and their highest nearby range cells (share 1.33–1.73) read 0.019–0.026 → 0.020–0.080, because the Earth preset's moisture is a quantile map of the observed rain and the driest 26 % of land sits at its 0.02 floor (raw annual moisture p25 = 0.020, p30 = 0.022): a ×1.5 share on a desert-range pixel does not move its rank out of the floor band. P18 acts where the range is wet — the Alps, the Pamir, the Tian Shan, the Hindu Kush, the Alborz crest (crest moisture +0.1–0.25, foot −0.05–0.15) — and not where the whole table cell is dry. So this row will not move under W14; the miss is now placed at the quantile map's floor band, a data-side finding recorded in QUESTIONS #66 and DECISIONS 35, and the floor is not to be lifted to reach it (second cardinal rule).
